prompt.context: BSN is the largest player in the Pre-Workout supplement category and owns a few major brands, including N.O. Xplode, Hyper FX, and Isoburn. Profitability of the pre-workout supplement category has been shrinking over health concerns associated with the product. However, vitamins and supplements as a whole are one of the fastest growing industries in the US, growing at 6% a year and projected to generate $16.4 billion in revenues in 2016, of which pre-workout supplements make only a very small portion. BSN is considering the possibility of getting into the Whey protein market. Whey protein is a post-workout supplement that aids in muscle recovery.
prompt.question: What considerations and options does BSN need to take into account when deciding if and how to enter the Whey Protein market?

clarifying_info.q: Is BSN focused only on the US market?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the firm's focus is just on the US market.
BSN is not cash constrained and has money to invest if it makes sense.

clarifying_info.q: What is BSN's target payback period?
clarifying_info.a: BSN would like to break even on their investment within 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: What market share can BSN expect in year one?
clarifying_info.a: Research has shown that BSN can expect 10% of the Whey Protein market in the first year.

exhibits.title: 2015 Post-Supplement Market Revenue and Profit Margins
exhibits.shows: A table showing 2015 revenue figures and profit margins for four segments of the post-supplement market: Casein Protein, BCAAs, Whey Protein, and Total Post Supplement Market. The Whey Protein profit margin is marked as unknown (X?).

exhibits.title: 2015 ISO Financial Information
exhibits.shows: A table showing key financial data for ISO, a competitor in the Whey Protein market, including price per unit, monthly units sold, variable cost per unit, and total annual fixed costs.

framework: Should BSN enter the market? — Analyze the Whey Protein Market (size, growth rate, barriers to entry), Competitor Landscape (number of competitors, market share, competitive response), and BSN's own capabilities (ability to produce, opportunity cost, cannibalization risk, distribution channel fit)

Profitability analysis — Revenue potential (number of whey protein users × consumptions per year × price per consumption) and Costs (fixed: overhead, factory, advertising; variable: raw materials, labor, transportation; plus investment cost)
How should BSN enter? — Three options: Build capability in-house, Joint Venture, or Merger/Acquisition

questions.prompt: What considerations and options does BSN need to take into account when deciding if and how to enter the Whey Protein market? (Framework question)
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure the answer around three pillars: (1) Market attractiveness — size, growth, barriers to entry; (2) Competitive landscape — number of players, market share, likely competitive response; (3) BSN's internal fit — production capability, opportunity cost, cannibalization of existing pre-workout products, distribution channel leverage. Then address entry mode: build in-house, JV, or acquisition. A strong candidate connects each bucket to a clear decision criterion.

questions.prompt: What steps would you take to understand whether the Whey Protein market in the US is attractive, and what is BSN's profit potential in its first year of operations?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify three areas to investigate: overall market size, market growth, and attainable market share/penetration rate. Once these three areas are named, present Exhibit 1. Candidate must ask for BSN's expected market share (10% in year 1) — do not volunteer this. Candidate should calculate the Whey Protein profit margin using a weighted average approach, then estimate BSN's year-one profit.

math.setup: Whey Protein profit margin is unknown. Use total market profit and subtract known segments to back-solve for Whey Protein margin. Then apply BSN's 10% penetration rate.
math.answer: Whey Protein profit margin = 17%; BSN year-1 profit ≈ $4.25M

questions.prompt: BSN is considering either building the capacity to produce Whey Protein in-house or acquiring a small player in the market. What considerations should BSN take into account when evaluating each option?
questions.guidance: Build in-house: Does BSN management have the knowledge to produce Whey Protein? What is the lead time to build capacity? What are the short- and long-term profitability implications? What is the basic cost/benefit? Acquisition: Is there a suitable small company to acquire? Does BSN have sufficient cash? What are the integration costs? Is there a cultural fit?

questions.prompt: BSN has determined that building Whey Protein capacity in-house would take a full year to enter the market and 10 years to break even. BSN has received more detailed projections from ISO (a competitor). Given the ISO data in Exhibit 2 and an acquisition cost of $1,000,000 (provide only if candidate asks for upfront investment), how long will it take BSN to break even if it acquires ISO?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate ISO's annual contribution margin, then subtract fixed costs to get annual profit, then divide the total investment (acquisition cost $1M + any noted upfront cost; note: the exhibit solution uses $3,000,000 as investment cost — provide $1,000,000 upfront investment when requested, and candidate should reconcile or the casebook answer key uses $3M total investment). Present Exhibit 2. Only reveal the $1,000,000 upfront investment cost when the candidate requests it. Encourage candidate to compare result against BSN's 5-year breakeven target.

math.setup: Use Exhibit 2 data: Price=$20, Variable Cost=$15, Monthly Units=15,000, Annual Fixed Costs=$200,000. Investment cost = $3,000,000 (provide $1,000,000 upfront cost when asked; total used in answer key is $3M).
math.answer: BSN will break even on the ISO acquisition in approximately 4.3 years, which is within the 5-year target.

recommendation: BSN should enter the Whey Protein market by acquiring ISO.
The Whey Protein market has high profit margins (17%) and the acquisition achieves breakeven in 4.3 years, meeting BSN's 5-year target.
risks: Potential integration issues (cultural fit, operational alignment).
Potential opportunity costs from diverting resources from the core pre-workout business.
next_steps: Begin integrating the firms and identify integration risks, including cultural alignment.
Identify growing customer segments to expand BSN's Whey Protein presence and capture additional market share.
